notes: HALFTONE, a strictly monochrome, single-page interactive almanac of the black-and-white image. Eight live instruments rendered entirely in the browser from code: an animated halftone sphere (hero), a tone-to-dot-area ramp with a magnified cell, an LPI frequency loupe, a dot-gain/TVI step wedge, a two-screen moire generator, a one-bit dithering bench (Bayer, Floyd-Steinberg, Atkinson), an AM-vs-FM stochastic comparison wipe, plus a type/palette specimen and an accessible glossary. No external images, fonts, libraries or network requests; one classic script (no modules, so file:// works), one stylesheet, one inline-generated SVG favicon. All imagery is canvas/SVG/CSS. Responsive, keyboard accessible, reduced-motion aware, static and deployable as-is. Known limitations: the hero and moire canvases are rasterised at display resolution and re-render at ~30fps, so they are approximate rather than print-accurate; the FM screen uses a uniform random threshold rather than a blue-noise mask; no build step or automated test suite was run beyond local rendering.
